newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-BEVAN LIFTS AUSTRALIA AFTER FOUR RUN-OUTS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BEVAN LIFTS AUSTRALIA AFTER FOUR RUN-OUTS.

text.p: Michael Bevan lifted Australia to a respectable 249 for six in the second one-day international against England at The Oval on Saturday after the tourists had done their best to self-destruct.
Four batsmen managed to run themselves out on an Oval pitch which looked full of runs, including openers Mark Taylor and Mark Waugh.
Bevan, ably assisted by Adam Gilchrist, kept admirably cool to score his second one-day international hundred.
He was unbeaten on 108 when the innings closed, scored off 129 balls with six boundaries.
Gilchrist, another left-hander, helped Bevan add 113 for the fifth wicket after the tourists had been reduced to 98 for four.

The Australian reserve wicketkeeper, who replaced Greg Blewett in the only change to the side who lost the first international, played neatly off his legs and scampered enthusiastically between the wickets to score a valuable 53.
Skipper Taylor's miserable international run continued when he was hopelessly run out for 11 after Mark Waugh ran, hesitated, then ran again after pushing the ball into the off.
Two balls later Waugh, who had driven three sumptuous boundaries, called for a chancy run and was run out for 25 by a direct hit from Robert Croft.
Steve Waugh departed for 24 when he was bowled by Croft while Michael Slater, dropped at slip off Croft by Nick Knight before he had scored, was the most culpable offender of all.
Slater pushed Croft into the off, set off for a non-existent run, and when Bevan failed to respond was run out by at least a metre as Phil DeFreitas uprooted the middle stump.
Ian Healy (seven) was the fourth run-out victim, courtesy of a fine throw from Graham Lloyd.
